title: Human-Agent Interaction in Synthetic Social Networks: A Framework for Studying Online Polarization

bias_targets.methodology: Manipulating the ratio of pro- versus contra-content (e.g., 70/30, 30/70, 50/50) in a simulated social media newsfeed and evaluating its impact on human participants' opinion change, engagement metrics, and self-reported perceived bias.

Prompting LLM-based agents with continuous opinion values (-1 to 1) to simulate polarized versus moderate discourse on a policy topic (Universal Basic Income), and evaluating human participants' perceptions of the agents' bias, emotionality, and group identity salience.
